question: Can typed synthetic threat models cross the real route and validator with bounded unassessed source provenance, without granting permissions or changing old workflows?
baseline: Sprint 5 unchanged; no technical analyzer. Existing SOC/governance compatibility checked separately.
treatment: New explicit experimental gateway, typed graph, local guidance and model-schema boundary; deterministic stubs in this suite
runtime: existing Python 3.13 venv; SQLite/embeddings not used
metrics: accepted legitimate inputs / predeclared input-valid cases
output rejections / predeclared invalid stub outputs
missing evidence reporting / required gap cases
false authority or approval promotion / forged-status cases
route response structure and source membership / returned cases
fixed input and source hash identities
judgments: Synthetic implementation-authored, not independent human adjudication. Category consistency means source label matches enum, not semantic precision. Prompt-copy quarantine is not live model injection resistance.
stop_conditions: unknown modified/untracked material outside protected exception
no provider substitutions or unjournaled inference
replay: Full deterministic replays only; preserve failed attempts. Never edit expectations after outcomes.
